landscape.say: For businesses: Commercial Security: Security film, with optional attachment systems, that slows smash-and-grab entry through storefront and lobby glass and keeps shattered panes in the frame until a glazier can replace them. Anti-Graffiti: Clear sacrificial film that takes tags, etching and scratchiti instead of the glass, then gets peeled and replaced for far less than a new pane. Decorative & Frosted Glass: Frosted, etched-look and printed films for office partitions, clinic windows and branded storefront glass, with cut lettering, logos, door markings and bird-safe patterns available on request. Solar Control: Solar control film for commercial curtain walls and large glazing, reducing heat gain and hot spots near the perimeter of south and west-facing floors without replacing any glass.

landscape.say: For homes: Heat Control: Film that rejects solar heat on the south and west glass that overheats during September and October, a real help in the many city homes that have no air conditioning. UV Protection: Nearly clear film that blocks almost all ultraviolet light to slow fading of hardwood floors, rugs, art and upholstery, even in fog-belt rooms where UV still gets through a thin marine layer. Privacy: Frosted, one-way and gradient films for lightwell windows, garden-level units, bathrooms and street-facing bays where neighbors and passersby can see straight in, chosen so the room keeps its daylight. Decorative: Etched, patterned and stained-glass-look films for entry doors, transoms and sidelights.

landscape.label: Why Window Film Here
landscape.title: San Francisco Microclimates and the Window Film They Call For
landscape.say: San Francisco is a small city with very different weather from one ridge to the next. On a typical July afternoon the Outer Sunset and the Richmond District can sit under a grey marine layer while the Mission, Potrero Hill and Dogpatch are in full sun. A window film that makes sense on a bright Bernal Heights hillside can be the wrong call for a foggy block near Ocean Beach, where owners care more about holding winter warmth than rejecting heat.

landscape.label: Local Know-How
landscape.title: San Francisco Rules That Touch Window Film Projects
landscape.say: Interior window film is usually not a permit item, but a few local rules still come up. Buildings in historic districts and designated landmarks go through Planning review for visible exterior changes, so a mirrored film that changes how a facade reads from the street deserves a check first. Neutral and lightly tinted films rarely draw attention.

landscape.say: Here's how an install works. First, start with the quote form: name the rooms or floors that give you trouble and the time of day it happens. Then, they visit, confirm measurements and identify the glass: single-pane, dual-pane, tempered, laminated or old annealed glass. On install day, they protect floors and sills, clean each pane, apply the film wet and squeeze out the solution. Finally, small haze or water pockets can show for a few weeks while the film cures, and it takes longer in cool, damp fog-belt weather.
